title: Grateful Dead Live at Star Theatre on 1970-03-08
source: SBD -> Master Reel -> Cassette -> Dat -> CD

ai_review.summary: Clear soundboard capture of an intimate show with standout Lovelight and Black Peter, but the unknown guest’s closing set drags the performance down.
ai_review.review: The recording is a well‑balanced soundboard tape that many reviewers describe as crisp and excellent for an SBD. Musically the concert shines early on – the acoustic “Black Peter” and a hot “Lovelight” are repeatedly praised – yet the surprise guest who takes over the last three songs is widely condemned, leaving the show feeling uneven. Overall the performance is enjoyable apart from that disruptive finale.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers love the sound quality and early part of the concert (show strength), but a strong negative reaction to the unknown singer’s closing songs lowers the overall score.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Crisp, well‑balanced SBD transfer; praised for clarity and lack of noticeable dropouts. No major technical complaints beyond normal tape hiss.

poor_songs: Impromptu Blues (aka Wake Me Shake Me) performed by the unknown guest
Closing three songs with the guest singer
show_quality.setlist_flow: Intimate venue and strong acoustic set early on, building a hot mid‑show, but the surprise guest’s appearance on the final three numbers disrupts the momentum and leaves many listeners dissatisfied.
